## 190. Which links a closure needs (K1)

Ren, 19 October 2026, after asking of `GrownFragmentation`'s three bypass theorems "why these numbers? is this really a proof?" and which of the module's theorems are general laws: "let's make these limited, non general laws, into general ones". The AI's answer to the first question: the theorems are kernel-checked proofs, but of one hand-built body (seven divisions from one position, a path of eight, the middle bond `(3,4)`, the end bond `(0,7)` joined), with the law behind them unstated. The answer to the second: of the module's 31 theorems, 14 hold for every input, and those are bookkeeping of the model's own steps, the correctness of its bounded search and rewrites of the supplied return; the two laws taken into the core on 15 October (`closure_iff_certified`, `not_within_of_closed`) and `Readout.no_judge_of_merged` are the general part; every claim about the bodies (every tree cut certified, the bypass, the cut that spends without fragmenting) was an example.

**The question.** What do the examples show in general? When does removing a link change a closure, what does joining a link add, and what about growth makes every link needed?

**The move.** Read the bonds as a relation among formations and the components as closures (`WithinClosure`, `Becoming.Feedback`). A cut is a relation with some links removed, a join a relation with one link added; growth by attachment is a list of links each of which brings in a formation that took part in no earlier link. Nothing is decided: a removed link is described by a relation `added` with `rel ∪ added` the relation before the cut, so no equality of links needs deciding.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Cuts`).
- **A cut changes no closure exactly where every removed link is bypassed** (`Cuts.Joined`, `Cuts.closure_unchanged_iff_bypassed`): for any relation `rel` and links `added`, every closure under `rel` with `added` joined is the closure under `rel` exactly where each link of `added` has its second end within its first end's closure under `rel`. For one link read both ways (`Cuts.Link`), this is that each end lies within the other's closure (`Cuts.link_cut_unchanged_iff`), and under a symmetric relation that one does (`Cuts.link_cut_unchanged_iff_of_symm`). Relations with the same links have the same closures (`Cuts.within_congr`).
- **Joining one link** (`Cuts.within_link_iff`): after a link between `a` and `b` is joined, `g` lies within `f`'s closure exactly where it did, or `f` reaches `a` and `b` reaches `g`, or `f` reaches `b` and `a` reaches `g`. The proof certifies the right side as a closed region holding `f`, with no symmetry and no decision.
- **Attaching an unlinked formation** (`Cuts.Unlinked`, `Cuts.within_of_unlinked`, `Cuts.not_within_unlinked`, `Cuts.within_attached_iff`): a formation that takes part in no link reaches only itself and is reached by nothing else, so attaching it by one link changes no closure among the other formations.
- **Every link grown by attachment is needed** (`Cuts.Links`, `Cuts.links_symm`, `Cuts.links_split`, `Cuts.links_of_mem`, `Cuts.Attaches`, `Cuts.Attaches.suffix`, `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once`, `Cuts.attached_link_separates`): in a list of links each attaching, to another formation, one that took part in no earlier link, each link is listed once, and removing any one leaves its ends apart, whatever came before or after it. The proof goes down the links attached later: each attaches a formation other than the cut link's ends, which by the attachment law changes no closure between them.
- **After one join, a grown link is bypassed exactly where the join crosses it** (`Cuts.joined_bypass_iff`, `Cuts.joined_cut_unchanged_iff`): with one more link joined between `a` and `b`, the ends `p`, `n` of a grown link are joined without it exactly where `p` reaches one of `a`, `b` and the other reaches `n` without it; and cutting the grown link then changes no closure exactly there.

**On the base** (`Becoming.Cuts`, namespace `Flow`). A formation's system is its closure under sharing a condition (`Flow.WithinSystem`, `Becoming.Feedback`), so the laws above read on the world's own relation.
- Sharing a condition is sharing one other than `c`, or both taking part in `c` (`Flow.SharesBeside`, `Flow.BothTakePart`, `Flow.shares_iff_beside`); splitting the two needs equality of conditions decided, given as `[DecidableEq C]`.
- **Which conditions a system needs** (`Flow.system_unchanged_without_iff`): every system is what it is through the other conditions alone exactly where any two formations taking part in `c` lie in one system through the other conditions. A condition only one formation takes part in is needed by no system (`Flow.system_unchanged_of_single`).
- **A condition two formations take part in** (`Flow.withinSystem_two_takers_iff`): where exactly `a` and `b` take part in `c`, `g` lies within `f`'s system exactly where it does through the other conditions, or `f` reaches one of them and the other reaches `g` through the other conditions. The reflexive pairs `c` adds change nothing (`Cuts.within_of_steps`).
- **Alone without its only condition** (`Flow.alone_beside_of_only`, `Flow.withinSystem_of_no_part`): a formation that takes part only in `c` reaches nothing else through the other conditions and nothing reaches it; one that takes part in no condition has only itself in its system.

**In the periphery** (`PreparationCorrespondence`, new section).
- The bonds read both ways are the listed links (`adjacent_iff_links`), so being connected is lying within their closure (`connected_iff_links`).
- A division attaches the new position by at most one bond, and every bond joins positions below the count (`AttachedBelow`, `divide_attached`), so whatever the division word, the bonds stay grown by attachment (`develop_attached`, `initial_attached`). Cutting a bond grown by attachment removes exactly it (`cut_attached`).
- So every bond of every body grown by division separates its ends when cut (`bond_cut_separates`, `every_grown_bond_separates`): the general form of `every_tree_cut_certified`, for every word rather than two.
- After one aggregation, cutting a grown bond changes no connection exactly where the aggregated bond's ends lie on its two sides (`aggregate_cut_unchanged_iff`), and the reinforced chain is a case: cutting `(3,4)` after joining `(0,7)` changes no connection, `0` lying on `3`'s side and `7` on `4`'s (`reinforced_cut_unchanged`). This is the general form of `bypass_survives_cut` and `bypass_really_connects`; the two sides are still computed for the chain.

**What this changes.** The example theorems become cases: a body grown only by division is a tree, every one of its bonds needed, and a single added bond makes exactly the bonds it crosses unneeded, which is why the reinforced chain's middle cut spends without fragmenting. The ranking and summary results keep their status: `no_parent_summary_predictor` already rests on `Readout.no_judge_of_merged`, and `oldest_cut_reverses_ranking` stays a counterexample showing that the ranking of the two bodies depends on the cut law. The computed pools, kinds and returns (`central_cut_pools`, `only_equal_tree_cuts`, `central_seed_properties`, `all_cut_returns`, `uniform_cut_returns`) are evaluations of the supplied rules on the two bodies and have no law beyond those rules.

*Reading* [AI reading, open]. A link is needed by a closure exactly where nothing else carries what it carries. Growth by attachment alone makes every link needed: such a whole holds together only through each of its links, and loses a part with any one of them. A link that closes a loop is what lets a whole lose a link and keep its closures; it makes needless exactly the links on the loop it closes. Whether keeping, cutting or adding links supports 生生 is not decided here.

**Not done.** Growth by attachment read on the base (a world in which each new formation takes part only in a condition shared with one earlier formation), so that the twelve laws of growth by a list of attachments stand on the base rather than apart; which links form or are cut, and when; what a cut or join takes (the model's budget stays a supplied law); several joins at once, beyond applying `Cuts.within_link_iff` repeatedly; counts (a grown relation's links one fewer than its formations); a general law for the cut returns; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `Cuts.closure_unchanged_iff_bypassed` certifies `WithinClosure rel f` as a region closed under the joined relation; the other direction is `WithinClosure.mono`.
- `Cuts.within_link_iff` certifies the three-way disjunction as closed under the joined relation; the link's two readings each move one disjunct to another, and `subst` is the only rewriting.
- `Cuts.within_of_unlinked` and `Cuts.not_within_unlinked` certify the regions `x = n` and `x ≠ n`; `Cuts.within_attached_iff` needs no premise `p ≠ n`.
- `Cuts.attached_link_separates` recurses on the later links; `Cuts.Attaches.listed_once` uses the same recursion with `List.Mem`'s two cases. All by structural recursion and `match`, so every declaration has an empty axiom report.
- The periphery section uses `simp`, `omega` and `List.append_of_mem`, so its theorems report `propext`, `Quot.sound` and in places `Classical.choice`; `AttachedBelow` and `initial_attached` have empty reports and are added to the checker's `EMPTY` list.
- `Flow.shares_iff_beside` decides `d = c` with the given `DecidableEq C` (a `dite`, no axiom); `Flow.withinSystem_two_takers_iff` sends each sharing through `c` to the link or to `WithinClosure.refl` by cases on the takers.
- The first connectivity measure found all 17 laws of the first draft apart: stated on any relation, used by nothing on the base. The base laws above were added so that the cut, join and attachment laws are read on the world's systems; twelve of the 24 stand on the base or are used there, and the three apart roots (the list-growth laws) are registered with their reason.
- Checker runs: core `20261019T052230.247441Z` passed (24 theorems, 31 declarations, empty reports; 263 core modules, 9,919 theorems); instance `20261019T052332.277017Z` passed (24 theorems, standard axioms only). Two earlier core runs and two instance runs, on drafts before the base laws, are not landed.
